items.followUp: What is meant by two bodies being in thermal equilibrium?

rubric.why: Identifies the temperature condition for thermal equilibrium.
rubric.description: States that the bodies have the same temperature.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that their temperatures are equal.

rubric.why: Identifies what happens to heat transfer in equilibrium.
rubric.description: States that there is no net flow of heat between the bodies.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that no net heat is transferred between them.

modelAnswer: Two bodies are in thermal equilibrium when they are at the same temperature.
There is no net flow of heat between them.

items.followUp: State four differences between mass and weight.

rubric.why: Assesses the difference in the types of quantities.
rubric.description: Mass is a scalar quantity, whereas weight is a vector quantity.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly contrasting scalar and vector.

rubric.why: Assesses the meanings of mass and weight.
rubric.description: Mass is the amount of matter in a body; weight is the gravitational force acting on it.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly distinguishing the definitions.

rubric.why: Assesses how mass behaves at different places.
rubric.description: Mass remains constant from place to place.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that mass does not depend on location.

rubric.why: Assesses how weight behaves at different places.
rubric.description: Weight depends on gravitational acceleration and can vary from place to place.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that weight varies with gravity or location.

modelAnswer: Mass is a scalar quantity, whereas weight is a vector quantity.
Mass is the amount of matter in a body, whereas weight is the gravitational force acting on it.
Mass remains constant from place to place.
Weight depends on gravitational acceleration and may vary from place to place.

items.followUp: A car has an initial velocity of 8 m/s and accelerates uniformly at 3 m/s^2 for 4 s. Find its final velocity.

rubric.why: Assesses identification of the given quantities.
rubric.description: Identifies initial velocity, acceleration and time.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct given values.

rubric.why: Assesses selection of the uniform-acceleration equation.
rubric.description: Writes the relation v = u + at.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct formula.

rubric.why: Assesses substitution using the given quantities and units.
rubric.description: Substitutes the values with units into v = u + at.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correct substitution with units.

rubric.why: Assesses the arithmetic result.
rubric.description: Calculates the final velocity as 20.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct numerical result.

rubric.why: Assesses the final answer and SI unit.
rubric.description: Gives the final velocity as 20 m/s.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct answer with unit.

modelAnswer: Given: u = 10 m/s, a = 2 m/s^2, t = 5 s
Answer: The velocity after 5 s is 20 m/s.

items.followUp: A force makes an angle of 60 degrees with the horizontal. If its horizontal component is 15 N, find the force.

rubric.why: Assesses identification of the horizontal component and angle.
rubric.description: Identifies the horizontal component as 20 N and the angle as 30 degrees.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct given values.

rubric.why: Assesses the component relation.
rubric.description: Uses horizontal component = F cos theta.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct relation.

rubric.why: Assesses rearrangement to find the force.
rubric.description: Rearranges the relation to F = F_x/cos(theta).
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct rearrangement.

rubric.why: Assesses substitution and numerical evaluation.
rubric.description: Substitutes the values and evaluates the force as approximately 23.1 N.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct substitution and numerical result.

rubric.why: Assesses the final answer with unit.
rubric.description: Gives the force as approximately 23.1 N.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct answer with unit.

modelAnswer: Given: horizontal component F_x = 20 N, angle theta = 30 degrees
Answer: The force is approximately 23.1 N.

items.followUp: A force of 60 N acts over a contact area of 2.0 cm^2. Calculate the pressure in pascals.

rubric.why: Assesses identification of force and area.
rubric.description: Identifies the force as 75 N and the contact area as 1.5 cm^2.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct given values.

rubric.why: Assesses the pressure formula.
rubric.description: Writes pressure = force/area.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct formula.

rubric.why: Assesses conversion of area to SI units.
rubric.description: Converts 1.5 cm^2 to 1.5 x 10^-4 m^2.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct area conversion.

rubric.why: Assesses substitution using SI units.
rubric.description: Substitutes force and converted area into P = F/A.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correct substitution.

rubric.why: Assesses the final pressure and unit.
rubric.description: Calculates the pressure as 5.0 x 10^5 Pa.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct answer with unit.
